title: The 1964 Great Alaska Earthquake and Tsunamis — A Modern Perspective and Enduring Legacies
summary: USGS Fact Sheet 2014–3018. How the M9.2 Good Friday earthquake — the largest in U.S. history — reshaped the coast, caused deadly local and Pacific-wide tsunamis, and helped prove that subduction zones make the world's greatest earthquakes.

title: Mount St. Helens — From the 1980 Eruption to 2000
summary: USGS Fact Sheet 036-00. The spring 1980 awakening, the May 18 landslide and lateral blast, the lahars, and the two decades of dome-building that followed.

title: The Orphan Tsunami of 1700 — Japanese Clues to a Parent Earthquake in North America
summary: USGS Professional Paper 1707, second edition (2015, with University of Washington Press; first edition 2005). How Japanese records of a tsunami with no felt earthquake, ghost forests and tree rings pinned the last great Cascadia earthquake to January 26, 1700.

title: The San Andreas Fault System, California
summary: USGS Professional Paper 1515. The classic book-length account of the San Andreas fault system: its geology, history, earthquakes and the plate motion behind it.

title: The Hayward Fault — Is It Due for a Repeat of the Powerful 1868 Earthquake?
summary: USGS Fact Sheet 2008–3019. The M6.8 1868 Hayward earthquake, the fault's ~140-year rhythm of large quakes, and what a repeat would mean for the San Francisco Bay region.

title: Earthquake Hazard in the New Madrid Seismic Zone Remains a Concern
summary: USGS Fact Sheet 2009–3071. Why scientists expect future large earthquakes in the central Mississippi Valley, from the 1811–12 sequence to the prehistoric sand blows that record older ones.

title: Steam Explosions, Earthquakes, and Volcanic Eruptions — What's in Yellowstone's Future?
summary: USGS Fact Sheet 2005–3024. Yellowstone's three caldera-forming eruptions, its earthquakes and hydrothermal explosions — and why the smaller hazards are the likelier ones.

title: PAGER — Rapid Assessment of an Earthquake's Impact
summary: USGS Fact Sheet 2010–3036. How USGS estimates fatalities and economic losses within minutes of a large earthquake — the green-to-red alert shown on Earth Alive's quake cards.
